summary.headline: Singer India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 37% to Rs 166.3 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 557 crore, up 29%, led by Sewing Machines.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 166.3 crore (up 37%), PBT of Rs 8 crore (up 43%) and EBITDA of Rs 9.3 crore (up 49%). For FY26, revenue was Rs 557 crore (up 29%), EBITDA Rs 21.5 crore (up 70%) and PBT Rs 17.3 crore (up 73%), after a one-time labour code cost of Rs 73 lakh; adjusted EBITDA was Rs 22.2 crore and adjusted PBT Rs 18.1 crore. Sewing Machines drove growth, while Appliances revenue grew about 10% in Q4 but its segment result fell by about Rs 2 crore. Management gave no formal guidance and did not answer questions on promoter exit or M&A.

segments.name: Sewing Machines
segments.commentary: Grew about 45% in Q4 and more than 40% for FY26; trade channel up about 20% in Q4 and over 15% for the year. Zigzag up over 30%, industrial up over 13% in Q4 and over 20% for FY26, cast-iron straight stitch and accessories up over 50% for the year. E-commerce up over 50% in Q4 and about 30% for the year.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 10% in Q4 on e-commerce range and fans, but segment result was lower by about Rs 2 crore due to EPR costs and fan business build-out. Demand muted, trade inventory blocked, dealer cash flows tight.

segments.name: Fans
segments.commentary: Fan business grew about 50% in Q4 with a new range covering economy, base, decorative, BLDC, TPW and exhaust fans; supply chain constrained by labour shortage and cost inflation.

guidance_outlook: Government (PMY) supply: more than 60% of the order completed; balance about 40% expected to be completed before the start of H2 FY27, though allocation timing has been revised.
Management intends to sustain sewing machine growth momentum but gave no numerical guidance.
Bhiwadi, Rajasthan factory (leased) expected to begin production in H2 FY27, initially focused on zigzag machines, with assembly first and components outsourced.
Management would not comment on future profits; said Appliances is expected to become profitable and that appliance challenges are temporary.
Management said the sewing machine business is expected to sustain growth, with the mix between sewing machines and appliances not expected to shift dramatically.
capex_capacity: Bhiwadi, Rajasthan factory: premises leased, production expected from H2 FY27, primarily zigzag machines; later capable of industrial machines and selected appliances.
Capex for new factory to be phased; could reach up to Rs 90 crore over 3 years, but not committed.
Assembly of zigzag machines has started in India; critical components to be made in-house once operations stabilise.
Acquired manufacturing rights from SVP in November 2025 for Rs 11.6 crore, amortised over more than 24 years.
Jammu factory now makes a full aluminium-body heavy-duty zigzag machine.
demand_pricing: Management estimates the total Indian sewing machine market at about Rs 3,000 crore: about 55% industrial, about Rs 700 crore straight stitch household, about Rs 350 crore artisan and about Rs 250 crore zigzag (management's estimate; not formal data). Market growing 4-6%.
Company mix for FY26: zigzag about 20%, classic black machines about 55%, industrial and accessories about 28-30%.
High-speed machines account for nearly 50% of Indian market revenue, per management.

New innovative machines (DSBB, SLBB, Link etc.) are about 15% of household sewing machine category. Tailor Mate, a motorised straight-stitch machine priced near classic black machines, is gaining traction.
Raw material inflation: PMY government orders are fixed-price and cost increases must be absorbed. Labour shortage and steep commodity price rises disrupted supply and demand in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Are PMY orders fixed-price, and can raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the orders are fixed-price and the company has to absorb the raw material cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fan business turn losses into breakeven in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no profit guidance; said fan sales grew about 50% in Q4, the heat is seasonal, and appliances will become profitable over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the government contract and when will it complete?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 60% of government supply is complete; the remaining 40% is expected before the start of H2 FY27. Growth came from government, retail and e-commerce.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for zigzag manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is phased and could reach Rs 90 crore over 3 years, but is not committed; the factory is leased and starts with assembly.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 not much higher than Q3 this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no specific reason; CFO said Q3 was about Rs 160 crore and Q4 about Rs 165 crore, and growth is expected to be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Should the PMY order completion target move from June 2026 to September 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply depends on allocations received; initial allocation estimates have been revised to a different pace. The second PMY order will come when government issues it.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pay a larger one-time dividend given cash and low ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the dividend should be seen in the context of a profitable journey and that cash will be deployed in opportunities, with no timeline. CFO said ROCE is almost 10%, with working capital improvement and the Bhiwadi capex ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter (Retail Holdings) planning to exit, and are there M&A talks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on exit talk or M&A, saying matters are confidential, and said the Board is supportive and fully involved.

risks_watch: Fixed-price PMY government orders: raw material and labour cost inflation must be absorbed, pressuring margins.
Appliances segment remains loss-making: segment result down about Rs 2 crore, with EPR costs, blocked trade inventory and weak dealer cash flows.
PMY allocation pace has slowed versus earlier estimates, so the completion timeline could slip beyond H1 FY27.
Cash of about Rs 83 crore (analyst figure) with no deployment timeline; shareholders pressing for a special dividend.
Unanswered questions on promoter Retail Holdings (India) BV exit and possible M&A; management declined to comment.
Bhiwadi factory and up to Rs 90 crore capex over 3 years: execution and returns not yet defined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sewing machine momentum and market share gains, but cautious and evasive on appliance profitability, dividend policy, cash deployment and promoter/M&A questions, which were declined or left without a timeline.
key_quotes: Strong growth consistently across all channels and categories demonstrates the success of our consistent efforts to excite the market with innovative products, deeper engagement with dealers.
We believe the challenges in Appliances are temporary, and the long-term opportunity in this segment remains significant.
We supply as many orders as we receive. It works in two parts.
